topics.answer: The work is named Deemed Contributions, Fee Waivers & Special Profits; the supplied procedure identifies it as FA-06.
The procedure produces updated member-level deemed contribution and commitment balances and a reconciled, approved period/event package.
The initiating event or notification, its recipient, cadence and fixed deadlines are not established by the supplied procedure.

The preparer and second reviewer reconcile member ICC, commitment, fee, event, capital-account, GL and GP records, confirm special-profits support, lock the source schedule and distribute the approved version. The period/event remains open for unresolved schedule or accounting divergence; one approved life-to-date version and zero unexplained differences are required.
The procedure identifies preparers and reviewers but does not identify the role ultimately accountable for the overall result.

The assigned Fund Administration preparer, with client/advisor input, identifies the fund, GP vehicle, members, effective date and fees; records the method and cash- and waiver-funded commitments by member; obtains written client and advisor confirmation; and designates the controlled life-to-date schedule.
The Fund Administration preparer rolls forward waived fees and deemed contributions by member and reconciles commitment balances to GP records and cumulative contributions and special profits to capital accounts and GL/TB. A second reviewer verifies; differences are resolved or documented before new activity, and version divergence is escalated.
The preparer confirms member eligibility with client confirmation, compares the population with the prior period and identifies departures, leave, exceptions and election changes. New waiver activity is suspended when employment status no longer qualifies, pending approved restructuring.
The management-fee preparer provides the approved period/event calculation; the receiving preparer validates gross fee, offsets, waiver, net fee and member allocation against dates, entity, approved version, arrangement and cumulative tracking. Unexplained differences are returned for resolution.
Using the approved waiver and eligible population, the preparer calculates deemed contributions by member, updates the life-to-date roll-forward, reduces approved waiver-funded unfunded commitment and updates GP capital and accounting support. Accounting/Fund Team posts as applicable; approved accounting direction is needed for unspecified entries and offsets.
The FA-06 preparer coordinates with the FA-01 event preparer to split each member's event allocation between waiver funding and cash due, update allocation and notice data, and reconcile the event to the ICC and GP unfunded schedules. Unclear disclosure or treatment is escalated to the client/advisor.
For special profits, the preparer identifies the fund method, timing, available-income definition, population and target adjustment, and obtains written advisor and client approval before calculation or entry. If the method is unspecified, the procedure requires a hold and advisor direction.
The preparer calculates and allocates special profits to the approved GP/member population, updates capital and event schedules and prepares the approved entry; a second reviewer checks and accounting/Fund Team posts. Allocations and recorded amounts are reconciled to the approved total; negative, excessive or unsupported results are escalated.
For departure or loss of eligibility, new waiver funding stops from the effective date unless written client/advisor direction says otherwise. Treatment may convert future waiver-funded commitment to cash or forfeit remaining waiver unfunded; any partner reallocation and schedule updates are reconciled to the approved post-departure structure. The procedure says not to assume the treatment.
At period/event reconciliation the preparer and second reviewer lock and distribute the approved source schedule and retain approvals and unresolved-item ownership.

The arrangement check requires support for every member, amount source, method and effective date; calculations are held if governing terms or advisor approval are missing. Opening reconciliation requires zero unexplained differences across the designated roll-forward, GP schedule, capital accounts and accounting.
The waiver input must trace to the approved fee calculation and not exceed the arrangement; no deemed contribution is recorded for an ineligible period/member without written advisor/client direction. The capital-event check requires cash due plus deemed/waiver funding to equal the approved allocation.
Special profits cannot shift without a supported method, available-income result and approval. Allocations must equal the approved total, satisfy available-income and capital-account limits and leave no unexplained residual.

The arrangement may use an LPA-dictated method, fixed schedule or waive-first-then-true-up; the preparer records the method and obtains written confirmation. Departure treatment also depends on the approved election rather than an assumed replacement or forfeiture.
The procedure warns that unclear employment-status sources, roles or timing can allow an ineligible waiver to continue or cause incorrect commitment allocation.

The supplied N03 FA-06 procedure pages describe the current route according to the participant. Working and retained artifacts include the arrangement summary, ICC/waiver roll-forward, approved arrangement and opening schedule, GP capital schedule, fee workpapers and GL/TB.
The procedure also uses a member-status schedule and change log, capital-call workbook, special-profits methodology record and available-income schedule, departure decision record, and period/event package. It requires retention of approvals and unresolved-item ownership.

The participant says the supplied procedure describes how the work is carried out today; the detailed steps below are sourced to that procedure.
The procedure covers funds, GP vehicles and eligible members, including member commitment funding, deemed contributions, special profits and changes in eligibility.

Governing documents, client approval and member/commitment data are prerequisites. A workbook, template, prior deliverable or recollection is a method or supporting record, not independent authority unless an approved policy is explicitly established.
The supplied procedure does not specify the special-profits formula or method, available-income definition, or exact accounting entries and offsets; approved direction is required rather than an assumed calculation.

The process consumes an approved management-fee calculation from the management-fee preparer and coordinates capital-event treatment with the FA-01 event preparer. The approved life-to-date schedule is distributed to dependent processes, whose destinations are not specified in the supplied text.

The procedure uses the ICC roll-forward as a designated life-to-date source schedule alongside GP schedules, fee workpapers, capital accounts and GL/TB. A capital-call workbook and special-profits schedules are also used; the supplied pages do not identify their storage locations or system of record.
